**Finding: missing (medium severity) — no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation.**

What I checked:
- **§17 (Term and Termination)** — runs one way only: Sparkling must cease use and certify destruction/return of Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes; §17(c) gives a perpetual-licence conversion plus refund on Garman default. No Garman obligation to return Sparkling's data or assist with exit.
- **§18 (Survival)** — lists §§13, 14, 15, 16(b), 18, 19, 20; no exit or data-return obligation to survive.
- **§16 (Source Code Escrow)** — Codes held on Sparkling's own AS400s; software continuity only, not data return, so only a partial substitute.
- **§4(b)** — confirms Garman does handle Sparkling's data (conversion tasks), so the gap is live, not theoretical.
- Text searches for "transition" and "data" surfaced no exit/export/deletion mechanic anywhere.

Because even the fallback (90 days' assistance + 30-day export) is absent, I inserted the preferred position as a new §17(d): up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in machine-readable form within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. The redline validated `ok:true` and the finding is submitted, with the 90-day fallback flagged in the comment as a landing zone.
